messages.subject: help in population density secr
messages.body_plain:
Hello, I am currently estimating the population density of Leopardus pardalis_ in Colombia.

During the analysis of results I have encountered challenges when executing the data in R studio, I work with the spatially explicit model of Bayesian capture - recapture, these challenges (problems) arise when executing the script they generate errors in the camera trap, I have reviewed several articles and I have not been able to find the solution to this challenge, in my University there is no one who knows about the subject or manages this model and who can help me.
I greatly appreciate your help and understanding, I will be attentive to your comments from your experience.

messages.subject: mark-resight and b compatability?
messages.body_plain:
I'm running a combined capture-mark-resight model and am having trouble incorporating learnt behaviour (b). Variance calculation fails (and 80% of the time R studio crashes, aborting the session, but I suspect that's an R issue not a secr issue).

I've tried different fit methods. Before I go too into detail trying to fix it, I wanted to check there weren't any known limitations with resight data with regards to learnt behaviour (b).

Thank you!
Tess

messages.subject: Re: mark-resight and b compatability?
messages.body_plain:
If running 'secr' causes R Studio to crash then 'secr' is responsible and need to be fixed (audible groans, as I don't enjoy mark-resight at the best of times). So could you please send an example, preferably small and simple?

Exactly how do you see a learned response working? is that within the capture phase, or between the capture and sighting phases? The latter sounds implausible, but I haven't thought deeply on it. However, it's natural to model different detection probabilities for capture and sighting (canned predictor 'ts'). There is no mechanism or code for a learned response from one sighting to the next.

Murray

messages.subject_clean: Predict by detector covariate and session
messages.body_plain:
Hi Cheryl
It probably helps to tighten up the terminology: you have one covariate Treatment with two levels 'Inside' and 'Outside'. In your case it should be enough to use
predict(fitted, all.levels = TRUE)
or more explicitly, for e.g. 5 sessions,
predict(fitted, newdata = expand.grid(session=1:5, Treatment = factor(c('Inside','Outside'))))
Murray

messages.subject: Density model with detector level covariate
messages.subject_clean: Density model with detector level covariate
messages.body_plain:
Good morning Murray,

I am new to SECR and still finding the ropes. I have a single-session camera trap dataset that I am analyzing to get a density estimate of leopards in the western cape of South Africa. I obtained a density estimate and I am now running inhomogeneous density models to get an idea of the factors driving density in the region. Without putting too much thought into it, I varied density by a variable (prey RAI) that I had calculated at each camera trap site (It is a detector level variable). The model ran successfully, however, after discussing this with a lecturer at my university, we could not work out how you can vary density across the study region with a detector level variable (rather than one embedded in the habitat mask)?
I was hoping you could help me understand how this would work (Does the model interpolate values for habitat cells between the detector sites)? or if I can still use the variable or perhaps a suggestion of how I could incorporate a variable like prey rai that I can only measure at camera sites?

Thank you and thanks for the awesome package.

Cheers,
Kyle

messages.subject: weird behavior/bug (?) in openCR lists
messages.body_plain:
Hi Murray,

I had some issues trying to streamline my code (using openCR models), when I explored the issue further I encountered a weird behavior of openCR lists that I don't understand. I modified one of your examples from openCR-examples.pdf to show what I mean. It is taken from page 2 (CJS) - see underneath. Example 1 throws a naming error when trying to extract AIC but Example 2 (adding another model) does work just as it is expected.

Maybe you have an idea what is happening, and how to avoid it happening?

Thanks a lot!!
Lukas

#openCR-examples _ example
#from page 2 CJS models
library(openCR)

#Example 1 -  does not work
args <- list(
  list(microtusFMCH, model = list(phi ~ sex+t, p ~ 1)),
  list(microtusFMCH, model = list(phi ~ t, p ~ 1)))

fits <- par.openCR.fit(args, ncores = 1)

AIC(fits)

#Example 2 - works
args <- list(
  list(microtusFMCH, model = list(phi ~ sex+t, p ~ 1)),
  list(microtusFMCH, model = list(phi ~ t, p ~ 1)),
  list(microtusFMCH, model = list(phi ~ sex+t, p ~ sex)))

fits <- par.openCR.fit(args, ncores = 1)

AIC(fits)

messages.subject: Re: Density model with detector level covariate
messages.subject_clean: Density model with detector level covariate
messages.body_plain:
A model for density should use mask covariates, so a detector-only covariate (your preyRAI?) should fail. You assert otherwise. Perhaps you could show the code and head(covariates(mask)) and head(covariates(traps(ch))) to convince us (and not just me - this is a group where anyone may chip in). Ad hoc interpolation/extrapolation of trap covariates at mask points can be done, but it's fairly ugly (see e.g. examples in ?skink).
